constraints: Python 3 standard library only; no installs and no network
synthetic data only; no real names or contact details
deterministic: the same input gives the same schedule
coverage_rules: Shifts are Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri and Sat, each with an AM and a PM slot: 12 shifts, written Day-Slot (for example Mon-AM).
Every shift has at least 2 volunteers.
Every shift has at least 1 volunteer whose role is lead.
A volunteer works only shifts listed in their available column.
No volunteer works more shifts in the week than their max_shifts.
No volunteer works both the AM and the PM shift on the same day.

deliverables.README.md: What the kit does, the input format, the coverage rules, how to run it, how to run the tests, and that it was built and tested on synthetic data only.
deliverables.shift_scheduler.py: Python 3 standard library only. Reads the CSV, builds a weekly schedule that meets every coverage rule (use a search such as backtracking: a simple first-fit pass can fail on this data), and writes it as CSV with columns shift,volunteer_id,display_name,role. Exposes check_coverage(schedule, volunteers) returning a list of violation strings (empty when every rule holds). CLI: python3 shift_scheduler.py data/availability.csv [--out schedule.csv] prints the schedule and the number of violations and exits 0 only when there are none; it exits 2 with a clear message when no valid schedule exists.
deliverables.tests/test_shift_scheduler.py: unittest tests: the synthetic CSV yields a schedule with zero violations; check_coverage reports each rule when it is broken (an unavailable volunteer, over max_shifts, no lead, both shifts on one day, fewer than 2 people); an impossible input is reported, not silently scheduled.

brief.need: We are a small food pantry (a synthetic example). Each week our volunteers tell us when they can come in. Please build us a small kit that turns our volunteer availability CSV into a weekly shift schedule that meets our coverage rules, with tests and a README, so our own agent or staff can run it. Use only the synthetic data provided.
